definitions.explanation: Noticeably different from the norm in a way that seems strange or quirky. Can describe people, things, or ideas.

examples.japanese: {風変|ふうが}わりな{人|ひと}だね。
{風変|ふうが}わりな{名前|なまえ}のレストランを{見|み}つけた。
examples.english: I found a restaurant with an unusual name.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}は{風変|ふうが}わりな{趣味|しゅみ}を{持|も}っていて、{古|ふる}い{地図|ちず}を{集|あつ}めている。
examples.english: He has an unusual hobby — he collects old maps.

notes:
Literally means "changed in style/manner" ({風|ふう} = style/manner + {変|か}わり = changed). Describes something that deviates from the norm, but without the strongly negative connotation that "strange" or "weird" might carry. Often implies mild curiosity or amusement.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {風変|ふうが}わりな{人|ひと}: an eccentric person
- {風変|ふうが}わりな{趣味|しゅみ}: an unusual hobby
- {風変|ふうが}わりな{建物|たてもの}: an unconventional building
- {風変|ふうが}わりな{考|かんが}え: an unconventional idea

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {変|へん}: strange, odd — more blunt, can be negative
- {独特|どくとく}: unique, distinctive — more neutral or positive
- {奇妙|きみょう}: bizarre, peculiar — stronger sense of strangeness
- ユニーク: unique — loanword, generally positive
